repo_notes.content: SCOPE — what this repository is and is not. YDelivery is an unofficial iOS client application for Yandex Delivery's Express (B2B Cargo) API, aimed at people and businesses sending parcels. It is not the API client itself: that is the separate YandexDeliveryExpress package, and anything about the API's own behaviour belongs there rather than here — do not re-document endpoints, request models or wire behaviour in this wiki. The app is unaffiliated with Yandex and deliberately carries no Yandex branding, which is a product decision, not an oversight. Two source trees carry the app: YDelivery/ and YDeliveryKit/. The design/ directory holds HTML, JavaScript and image design prototypes — visual exploration, not shipping code, and not a web front end. Several root-level Markdown files are process artefacts rather than product documentation and should not each become a page: CLAUDE.md is agent instructions, REVIEW.md is a review record, and DESIGN-HANDOFF.md, Design-Research-Brief.md, Design-Research-Dossier.md and Positioning.md are research and handoff material.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES, in precedence order. The DocC catalogue at YDelivery/Documentation.docc/ is authoritative for this app's direction and outranks README.md, which says so itself: Vision.md states what the app is and carries the capability map from API surface to feature to phase, Design.md holds the load-bearing decisions each with its rejected alternative, Roadmap.md the priority order phase by phase, TechDebt.md every compromise carried under a YD-n identifier, and DesignSystem.md and LinkGrammars.md the presentation and navigation conventions. For anything about the API itself the sibling package's catalogue is authoritative, starting with its Working with the Yandex API article. README.md is the entry point and the build runbook.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: CONSTRAINTS a reader must not miss. The app requires iOS 17 and a recent Xcode, and the project is generated by XcodeGen rather than committed, so regenerate before building. The product framing is load-bearing and should shape how features are described: the sibling YandexDeliveryExpressDemo exists to demonstrate the package honestly with its rough edges showing, whereas this app is the product bet and the user is never shown a raw API concept such as a claim. The API it talks to has no published OpenAPI document — the package's specification is hand-written and validated against live traffic — so any statement about API behaviour is an observation with a date behind it rather than a contract, and should be described that way.
repo_notes.author: maintainer
